+# Smoke Test: Codex Engine Validation

+**IMPORTANT: Keep all outputs extremely short and concise. Use single-line responses where possible. No verbose explanations.**

+

+2. **Safe Inputs GH CLI Testing**: Use the `safeinputs-gh` tool to query 2 pull requests from ${{ github.repository }} (use args: "pr list --repo ${{ github.repository }} --limit 2 --json number,title,author")

+- PR titles only (no descriptions)

Update smoke-codex.md post-steps to detect permission-blocked write
actions (common in PR runs with read-only permissions). When permissions
are blocked, the safe-output validation is relaxed instead of failing.

The .md source is updated (not just the lock file), and the lock file
is properly recompiled via gh aw compile + postprocess.

   - name: Validate safe outputs were invoked
     run: |
       OUTPUTS_FILE="${GH_AW_SAFE_OUTPUTS:-${RUNNER_TEMP}/gh-aw/safeoutputs/outputs.jsonl}"
+
+      # Detect permission-blocked writes (PR runs with read-only permissions)
+      PERMISSION_BLOCKED=false
+      for LOG_FILE in "/tmp/gh-aw/agent-stdio.log" "${RUNNER_TEMP}/gh-aw/agent-stdio.log"; do
+        if [ -f "$LOG_FILE" ] && grep -qE 'blocked by permissions in this environment|GraphQL operation denied' "$LOG_FILE"; then

* Initial plan

* fix(api-proxy): handle missing leading slash and body-shape guard in injectStreamOptions

* fix: use --build-local in all workflows to test from source

Cherry-picks the postprocess script fix that replaces standalone
--skip-pull with --build-local, ensuring CI builds all containers
(including api-proxy) from source code. This is critical for testing
the stream_options.include_usage fix on this branch.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(api-proxy): strip unrecognized tool types from Responses API requests

Codex CLI v0.133 registers MCP tools with type: "custom" which OpenAI
Responses API rejects (400 "Invalid value: custom"). The api-proxy now
strips tools with unrecognized type values before forwarding, similar
to how stream_options.include_usage is already handled.

Known-good types: function, code_interpreter, web_search_preview,
web_search, file_search, computer_use_preview, mcp.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* api-proxy: strip encrypted include for model incompatibility

Codex CLI v0.133 unconditionally requests reasoning.encrypted_content
in the include parameter for all models, but some models reject this
with 400 'Encrypted content is not supported with this model.'

Add stripEncryptedInclude() transform that removes encrypted-related
include values for Responses API requests. Log includes the model name
and a clear explanation that this is a model/feature mismatch.

This is a defensive workaround — the client should ideally check model
capabilities before requesting encrypted content.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* smoke-codex: default model to gpt-5.3-codex

gpt-5.5 (Codex's auto-selected default) rejects reasoning.effort and
encrypted content parameters. The gpt-5.3-codex model is purpose-built
for Codex and supports these features.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(api-proxy): strip reasoning params rejected by API key tier

Codex CLI sends reasoning.effort unconditionally, but the CI API key
tier does not have access to reasoning features, causing 400 errors
for all models (gpt-5.5, gpt-5.3-codex, etc.).

Two-pronged fix:
1. Set model_reasoning_effort = "none" in Codex config.toml to tell
   Codex not to send reasoning params at all
2. Add stripReasoningEffort() body transform in api-proxy as
   belt-and-suspenders defense against any client sending unsupported
   reasoning parameters

Also updates postprocess script to inject model_reasoning_effort
idempotently on recompile.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ci): remove model_reasoning_effort=none, rely on api-proxy strip

Setting model_reasoning_effort="none" in config.toml caused gpt-5.3-codex to
produce no output (38s timeout with empty response). The model likely needs its
default reasoning mode to function.

Instead, rely solely on the api-proxy stripReasoningEffort() transform which
removes the reasoning.effort field at the wire level before OpenAI sees it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ci): switch smoke-codex to gpt-4.1 for API key compatibility

The CI API key can list gpt-5.3-codex in /v1/models but cannot actually
use it for inference — requests hang indefinitely with no response.
Switch to gpt-4.1 which is widely available across all API key tiers.

fix: broaden GHES detection for Copilot auth prefix (#5076)

* fix: broaden GHES detection for Copilot auth prefix

The api-proxy previously only detected GHES when the resolved target was
exactly 'api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com'. When COPILOT_API_TARGET is
set to a custom hostname (e.g. by older gh-aw versions or custom
configurations), the check failed and Bearer was sent instead of token.

Add isGhesInstance() that checks multiple signals with clear priority:
  1. AWF_PLATFORM_TYPE=ghes (explicit config, highest priority)
  2. Resolved target === api.enterprise.githubcopilot.com
  3. GITHUB_SERVER_URL not github.com / *.ghe.com

a 'type' field that explicitly declares the deployment environment
(github.com, ghes, ghec, ghec-self-hosted). This is forwarded as
AWF_PLATFORM_TYPE to the api-proxy container, giving users a definitive
way to control auth behavior without relying on heuristic detection.

ci: add required supply-chain scan on every PR (#6530)

* ci: add required supply-chain scan on every PR

Add a deterministic (non-agentic) workflow that runs
`gh aw compile --strict --syft --grype --grant` on every pull request.

The Anchore scanners run via Docker against the container images recorded
in the compiled `*.lock.yml` manifests:
- --syft:  generate an SBOM per image
- --grype: scan for known CVEs / insecure libraries
- --grant: enforce the license allowlist in `.grant.yaml`

`--strict` makes any finding or scan error fail the job so it acts as a
real gate. Add `.grant.yaml` at the repo root since `--grant` requires it.

The "Compile + Syft/Grype/Grant" check is added to the "CI passes before
merging to main" ruleset so it is required before merge.
